title: INTC, AMD Slide Premarket After Nvidia Unveils New PC Processor – Intel’s Xeon 6 Data Center CPU Launch Overshadowed
key_facts: Intel and AMD shares fell about 4.2% in premarket trading on Monday after Nvidia unveiled its first PC processors.
At Computex 2026 in Taipei, Nvidia said it built the N1X processor with Microsoft; it goes into the RTX Spark chip in Windows PCs from Microsoft, Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo and MSI this fall.
Intel and AMD have long dominated PC chips built on x86 designs; Nvidia's chip is Arm-based.
Intel unveiled the Xeon 6+ server chip on its 18A process at the same show and claimed about 30% better per-thread performance than AMD's 192-core Epyc 9965.
Intel said its next server line, Xeon 7 (Diamond Rapids), is slated for 2027.
quote_evidence: Shares of Intel and Advanced Micro Devices fell about 4.2% in premarket trading on Monday, amid competitive concerns after Nvidia unveiled its first PC processors, entering a market long dominated by the two chipmakers.
The chipmaker unveiled the Xeon 6+ CPU, built using Intel's most advanced 18A process.
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia entering PC processors puts pressure on the two firms that have long supplied them.
notes: Article cites Computex 2026 and a Monday premarket move, but is listed as published 4 Oct 2026; Computex is held in early June, so this looks like older news re-dated. Date inferred, not stated. Share-move line mixes up AMD/INTC year-to-date figures, so not used.
